s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations in a pregnant patient with regular narrow QRS tachycardia
salient_findings: Regular cannon waves on jugular venous pulsations
key_facts: Patient is a primigravid in their 20s
In eighth month of gestation
Palpitations lasted for a few minutes and subsided spontaneously
No associated sweating, syncope, dyspnoea, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
Blood pressure was 110/70 mm Hg
Heart rate was 120 beats/min
Jugular venous pulsations revealed regular cannon waves
Auscultation was significant for a variable first heart sound
Laboratory tests were within normal limits
2-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography showed good biventricular function and normally functioning valves
ECG showed regular narrow QRS tachycardia at a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min

shortlist.why_kept: Regular narrow QRS tachycardia with variable PR intervals

shortlist.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Regular narrow QRS tachycardia with regular P waves

shortlist.label: Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Palpitations lasting a few minutes and subsiding spontaneously

shortlist.label: Atrial Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Regular cannon waves in jugular venous pulsations

shortlist.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of regular narrow QRS tachycardia in a young patient

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of episodic palpitations, regular narrow QRS tachycardia on ECG, and variable first heart sound are consistent with Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (PSVT). The presence of regular cannon waves in the jugular venous pulsations also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: Although a type of PSVT, the ECG findings do not specifically point to AVNRT as the primary diagnosis without further electrophysiological testing.

rejected.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: This condition is often associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, which is not indicated by the ECG description provided.

rejected.label: Atrial Flutter
rejected.why: The ECG description does not match atrial flutter, which typically shows a sawtooth pattern of P waves.

rejected.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
rejected.why: The ECG description does not mention a delta wave, which is characteristic of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: The diagnosis of AVNRT requires more specific electrophysiological criteria that are not provided in the case description.
